title: Finite morphisms are integral, and locally finite type integral morphisms are finite

difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma with its two sentences: a finite morphism of algebraic spaces is integral, and an integral morphism which is locally of finite type is finite (source lines 9431-9436). The proof notes that in both cases the morphism is representable and that the conditions may be checked after base change by an affine scheme mapping into the target, and then invokes the corresponding equivalence for morphisms of schemes.
